entries.title: Get hands-free personalized help on the road with Gemini
entries.summary: Center of image is a photo of a 1st-person point of view of driving a car. On the circumference of the circle are the Gemini logo and various prompts. The bottom of the image has the text "Personal Intelligence hits the road".
entries.content:
Gemini — your helpful AI assistant — is now available globally on Android Auto and cars with Google built-in. With Gemini, you can speak naturally to get more done or brainstorm ideas while driving.

An assistant is even more helpful when it knows the world and knows you. That’s why we’re rolling out Personal Intelligence with Gemini starting today, 1 to give you uniquely tailored answers and make Gemini even more valuable on the road.

With your permission, Personal Intelligence securely connects information from the Google apps you already use — Workspace (including Gmail and Google Calendar), Google Photos, Google Maps, YouTube, and Search.

Just ask — Gemini gets it

Personal Intelligence has two core strengths: retrieving specific details from, say, an email, photo or a place you saved in Google Maps to answer your question and reasoning across complex sources. That’s especially helpful when your hands are on the wheel. Personal Intelligence does the heavy lifting so you can speak naturally, without having to explain context or dig for information. Here are a few examples.

  • Make complex requests: On your way to the airport, ask, “What's my flight gate? And is my flight on time?” You don’t have to hunt for the confirmation email, then do a separate search for delays. Gemini gives you both answers in one go.
  • Get personalized picks every time: Looking for dinner in an unfamiliar town? Say, “Find me an indoor restaurant along my route that matches my usual vibe.” If you're vegetarian, you'll get a shortlist of places that fit your needs.
  • Speak naturally: Heading to an appointment? Say, “Take me to my doctor’s appointment.” You don’t have to remember the street address or look it up before you drive.
  • Retrieve details without pulling over: Trying to return to a place you saw earlier? Say, “Find the car wash from the photo I took last week and navigate there.” You don’t need to scroll through your camera roll or pull over to get the name and directions.
  • Pick up where you left off: Heading out for the morning? Say, “Take me to the coffee shop we were talking about yesterday”. Gemini will handle the digging and send you on your way.

Share only what you want

We built Personal Intelligence with privacy at the center. Your apps aren’t connected until you choose to turn it on, and you can turn it off anytime in your Gemini settings. And cars with Google built-in only share personal responses when you’re in the car with your phone connected. If you don’t use Personal Intelligence, everything in the car still works: You can use navigation, listen to music, make calls, and ask questions, but the answers won't be tailored to you.

Get started

Personal Intelligence is rolling out starting today 1 on Android Auto and in the coming months on cars with Google built-in. If you've already enabled it in the Gemini app, it comes with you into the car. If you haven't, you can set your preferences anytime in your Gemini settings.

entries.title: Ask a Scientist: How can AI help doctors spend more time on collaborative care?
entries.summary: Two Googlers in a virtual interview with text to the left of them that says 'Ask a scientist about patient care research'
entries.content:
Imagine showing up for an urgent care visit, and there’s no paperwork to fill out. Your doctor already has the details, because you chatted with an AI agent after booking your appointment. That agent went further than the one-size-fits-all questions you’d find on a standard intake form, asking you targeted follow-ups based on the personalized details you provided. Those specifics mean your doctor can spend less time information-gathering and more time on collaborative care: addressing your concerns, diagnosing your symptoms, and figuring out what to do next.

Google researchers are building that system. It’s called AMIE (Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer). And recent studies have shown the difference it can make for patients and doctors alike.

We sat down with research scientists Anil Palepu and Mike Schaekermann to learn more.

What do you do at Google?

Anil: We’re both research scientists on the AMIE team. I do a lot on the technical side — evaluating the AI agent, preparing it for studies, and expanding it so it can have real-time conversations over audio and video, not just text.

Mike: My work mostly involves planning clinical studies, building partnerships with healthcare providers, and submitting our research to journals.

What is AMIE, exactly?

Mike: AMIE is Google’s flagship research project exploring the future of AI in healthcare. We envision what’s possible — and see if we can make that a reality.

In this case, we wanted to train an AI agent to have clinical conversations. At the outset of our research, we envisioned something you could talk to any time you wanted, as long as you wanted, about your health concerns. And it would act like a bridge between you and your doctor, carefully synthesizing and sharing the information you’ve given it. That way, at your next appointment, your doctor could maximize their time with you.

How can AMIE potentially change the average doctor’s appointment?

Anil: AMIE is more targeted and more thorough than a standard doctor’s office intake form.

Let’s say I come in with back pain. While an intake form might ask me to describe the problem and check a few boxes, AMIE can ask follow-ups. What kind of pain? When did it start? Where is it in my back, exactly? That gives the doctor a better understanding of why I’m there, giving them more time to dig into potential causes and work with me to develop a treatment plan.

Mike: Doctors have told us AMIE helps them shift from gathering information to collaborating more with patients. When doctors don’t have to spend so much of their time verifying baseline facts, they can focus on discussing treatment options and making decisions with the patient.

Tell me more about your research. How did it work?

Mike: Study participants had the option to chat with AMIE before their next doctor’s appointment. AMIE took their clinical history and shared a concise summary with their physician. We had a trained physician oversee every AMIE-patient interaction just in case something unsafe happened, and they never had to interrupt the conversation or intervene.

What’s next for AMIE?

Anil: We’re working on a follow-up study that builds on what we’ve done so far. We want to see how well AMIE works on a much broader scale, across all of the US, with even more patients and involving controlled comparisons.

Mike: We also want to expand AMIE so the patients in our studies can interact with it in more ways. AMIE started as a text chat. Then, patients could share pictures in that text chat. And now we’re exploring what’s possible with video, so we can test how it works when patients talk to it out loud and show it what they’re experiencing.

What do you hope people take away from your work?

Mike: We want to enable everyone, everywhere to live their healthiest lives. And we believe systems like AMIE can give physicians back crucial time with their patients. This was a chance for us to show what AMIE can do in a rigorous way and hopefully build trust with the medical community.

Anil: So far, the evidence has demonstrated benefits for patients and doctors — and potentially, for the healthcare system as a whole.

entries.title: New Gemini tools for small business owners
entries.summary: "Your brand, your tools, all in one place" banner featuring three feature highlights: "Create image styles for your brand," "Customize Gemini with apps and skills," and "Create content with templates."
entries.content:
Tens of millions of small business owners are using Gemini today to brainstorm future products, manage customer feedback, and analyze business performance. Today, we’re announcing new tools designed to give these entrepreneurs their time back so they can focus on what started it all: their passion.

A central hub for small businesses owners, all in Gemini

We’re introducing a new business landing page designed to help small business owners streamline their daily tasks. From this central hub, they can build their brand, analyze finances, understand customer insights, and more.

We’re also making it easy to connect Gemini to Google tools like Google Business Profile, Google Ads, and Google Workspace, as well as third-party connected apps like Adobe, Canva, Dropbox, Shopify, Wix, Zoho, and Xero.

On-brand visuals

Businesses can now define their brand style in Gemini by uploading their website, brand kit, fonts, or color palettes. When paired with the power of Nano Banana 2.1 (our latest image generation model), Gemini can now deliver end-to-end visual results for new product launches or ongoing marketing campaigns. Gemini retains this visual style, allowing owners to easily generate cohesive, on-brand assets without having to repeatedly upload their style guidelines.

Real-time financial insights

Gemini can turn messy spreadsheets, receipts, and purchase records into clear financial graphics and interactive models in seconds. Instead of decoding numbers on their own, small business owners can receive financial insights in a more natural way.

Stories from small business owners around the world

The business landing page, marketing and finance skills, and new connected apps are beginning to roll out in the coming days globally for all Gemini app users.

And for larger businesses looking to scale AI across teams with centralized administrative controls, advanced data governance, and enterprise-grade security, explore Gemini for your business.

entries.title: Expanding our defenses against financial scam ads
entries.summary: Blue shield with a lock inside of it. In the background are the USA and Canada flags.
entries.content:
When you see an ad on Google, you should know who’s behind it. In both the United States and Canada, more than 97% of the ads people see on Google already come from identity-verified advertisers. 1 We’re building on this foundation by introducing Financial Services Verification in these North American markets, expanding a program that currently protects approximately 2 billion internet users across 42 countries from financial scams — the broadest program of its kind.

A proven, multi-layered approach to safety

When you're opening a checking account or looking for a credit card, trust is essential. That's why we're introducing additional protections to ensure these ads come from authorized financial providers.

On top of identity verification, our longstanding first line of defense, Financial Services Verification adds a specialized check to validate an advertiser's credentials. Under this policy, advertisers must demonstrate they are authorized by relevant regulators or recognized registries before running certain financial ads — helping prevent brand impersonation and stopping bad actors from reaching people. This builds on our work as the first major platform to require this type of verification, starting in the United Kingdom in 2021 and most recently expanding across the European Union.

Upfront advertiser verification works hand-in-hand with our safety systems. In 2025, Gemini helped our systems catch over 99% of policy-violating ads before they ever served, blocking bad ads in real time.

Cross-sector collaboration

Effective ad safety takes cross-industry coordination. Alongside our ongoing work with financial regulators, we're working in the U.S. with the American Bankers Association to use their dedicated registry to verify authorized banks before ads can run. In Canada, we’re engaging closely with the Canadian Bankers Association as we prepare for our rollout.

Because regulations differ across borders, we’re adapting our approach for each country through a phased implementation, protecting consumers while ensuring legitimate institutions can reach the people they serve. This work complements broader efforts like the Global Signal Exchange, where we share information across tech, finance, and law enforcement to stop fraud.

What advertisers can expect

Ahead of our planned rollout in early 2027, we’ll provide country-specific information for advertisers, including accepted registries, required credentials and onboarding instructions. Once verification opens, advertisers will be notified if and when they need to complete the process, ensuring businesses have the guidance they need to comply before policy enforcement begins.

Strengthening protections against financial scams in the U.S. and Canada is another important step in our ongoing work to keep our advertising platforms safe, transparent, and dependable for everyone.

entries.title: Partnering to strengthen the grid and support local communities in Arkansas
entries.content:
Since we first announced plans to build in West Memphis, Arkansas, we’ve continued to work directly with local leaders and community members to chart a path for responsible development. Today, we're announcing our next steps forward in that journey.

We are distributing the first $1.25 million guided by the on-the-ground expertise of our local Energy Impact Fund Council as a part of our $25 million West Memphis Energy Impact Fund. These grants will help support 10 local nonprofit and municipal organizations to increase clean energy access, lower home utility costs, and create new workforce opportunities in the region. Here’s what they plan to do:

  • CERTcuit, Inc.: Deliver career mobility training to 135 low- and moderate-income residents through industry credentials in IT, cybersecurity, cloud computing, and project management, supplemented by energy auditing and solar fundamentals.
  • East Arkansas Youth Services, Inc.: Implement the Energy Ready Families Initiative in Crittenden County, providing household energy assessments, efficiency upgrades, resource navigation, and workforce readiness for at-risk youth and up to 60 families.
  • Families in Transition, Inc.: Relocate and renovate an emergency shelter to increase capacity while implementing critical energy-efficiency upgrades, including roof replacement, insulation, air sealing, LED lighting, and HVAC modernizations.
  • Groundswell, Inc.: Scale the Google-supported SOUL (Save On Utilities Long-Term) program in West Memphis to provide energy efficiency upgrades and essential structural repairs for income-qualified households on its waitlist, while expanding local contractor delivery capacity.
  • IAP Ministries: Execute the Stay Safe at Home West Memphis program, delivering in-home assessments, energy-efficiency measures, and minor home repairs to 50 low-income households, prioritizing seniors, veterans, and residents with disabilities.
  • Junior Achievement of Memphis and the Mid-South: Expand career readiness and work-based learning pathways — including industry exposure, mentorship, internships, and apprenticeships — connecting local students to careers in energy, utilities, construction, advanced manufacturing, and infrastructure.
  • Life Empowerment Center: Drive the Trades for Life Teens Program, engaging youth ages 12-18 in hands-on trade training (electrical, HVAC, plumbing, carpentry) combined with mentorship, financial literacy, leadership, and energy education.
  • Producing Outstanding People: Launch the “Flip the Switch” initiative across Crittenden County, distributing energy-efficiency kits and affordable education alongside youth and adult programming in STEM, financial literacy, and career exploration.
  • The City of Earle: Establish a municipal Electric Rebate Program to subsidize home energy audits, HVAC, insulation, weatherization, and renewable energy upgrades for vulnerable, lower-income households while integrating local workforce development.
  • The City of Memphis: Pilot the One Front Door Operations Hub, creating a centralized entry point for residents seeking home repair and weatherization services through integrated intake, cross-program case management, and coordinated service delivery.

In addition, we’re continuing our partnership with Entergy Arkansas by investing in new energy and grid infrastructure that will strengthen the power system for all of its customers.

We’re grateful to the people of West Memphis for welcoming us, and we look forward to continuing to listen, learn, and work alongside local leaders to support a strong community for everyone.

entries.title: How to shape your slides and videos with Gemini Notebook
entries.summary: Illustration showing new review slide deck capabilities
entries.content:
Based on your feedback, Gemini Notebook now offers more creative control from start to finish on two of our popular outputs: Slide Decks and Video Overviews.

Instead of jumping from an initial prompt straight to a final output, Gemini Notebook can now walk you through the creation flow in a quick process based directly on your sources.

Steer your content

Start in the chat and ask Gemini Notebook to create slides or a video overview for you. Based on your sources, Notebook will suggest topics to be included in your artifact. Once you confirm, you will be able to steer the content further and guide visual style and format.

If you want to have even more creative control, you can use our new Review toggle. With this on, you can review the plan in the studio panel by clicking “Review outline notes” for slides and "Review producer notes” for video, plus give additional feedback, like asking to include an executive summary at the beginning or swapping the order of a scene, before anything renders. Once everything looks right, select “Proceed” to produce a final artifact.

Co-creation Slides walkthrough

Co-creation Video Overview walkthrough

Have Notebook take a first pass

If you already know what you want to create, you can specify this in your prompt and the notebook will go straight to the review flow.

If you prefer a quick output, you can still just go to the studio panel, click your artifact, skip the review toggle and have Notebook generate the artifacts, as usual.

These co-creation capabilities are rolling out globally to all Gemini Notebook users over the upcoming week.

entries.title: 4 tips for styling outfits with Gemini
entries.summary: UI showing a user asking Gemini to put a person into various outfit items
entries.content:
Sydney Bordonaro styles top professional athletes, turning the pregame tunnel into a must-watch runway. But because her roster is scattered across the country, being in the same room as clients for a fitting rarely happens. That makes her biggest challenge selling the vision. A photo of a jacket tells a player nothing about how the outfit actually looks on them, and when they can't see the idea, it’s easy to say no. That’s why Sydney uses Gemini to bring her ideas to life before an outfit ever ships.

Here’s how she builds looks for clients from hundreds of miles away:

1. Visualize the look.

Sydney uploads pictures of the clothes she sources to visualize them on her client directly in Gemini. It keeps the player looking like herself while showing how the full outfit comes together on her.

Try it yourself: Upload a photo of yourself alongside screenshots of items you want to buy. Gemini combines them into a single image so you can see how the full outfit looks before ordering.

2. Swap individual pieces.

Styling rarely lands on the first try. Sydney simply talks to Gemini to tweak details like swapping boots for loafers or cropping a jacket without having to start over from scratch.

Try it yourself: Instead of writing a new prompt, ask for single adjustments like "keep this outfit, but change the jacket to dark denim."

3. Get a second opinion.

Once the look comes together, Sydney sends the picture directly to her client. Seeing the complete fit builds confidence, often turning a hesitant "maybe" into a quick yes for bolder style choices.

Try it yourself: Test outfit ideas for upcoming weddings, job interviews, or trips and share them with friends for a gut check before you commit.

4. Rescue an outfit on the go.

Beyond building outfits, Sydney uses Gemini as a quick problem-solver. When an unexpected makeup smudge lands on a client’s collar right before an event, snapping a quick picture brings up specific, step-by-step instructions to clean it using stuff Sydney already has in the room.

Try it yourself: Take a photo of a clothing stain and ask Gemini how to clean it using what you have around the house.

Sydney brings the vision, the personal style, and the bold choices. Gemini is how she gets what’s in her head onto the screen so her clients can see it for themselves.

entries.title: See the top style searches from people in big fashion capitals.
entries.summary: We took a look at Google Trends to see what people in seven major fashion capitals are searching for to give them that je ne sais quoi when it comes to their sartorial s…
entries.content:
We took a look at Google Trends to see what people in seven major fashion capitals are searching for to give them that je ne sais quoi when it comes to their sartorial sensibilities. According to the data, people are experimenting with new silhouettes, clever styling hacks, hands-on alterations, and more. Here are a few trending takeaways:

  • In London and Milan, searches for empire waist dresses are reaching new highs.
  • Searchers in New York and São Paulo are turning to silk scarves as tops and shawls.
  • Creative layering and robust footwear queries are spiking in Copenhagen.
  • In Tokyo and Paris, ballet flats and loafers are dominating footwear searches.
  • Designer hair accessories and headbands are trending in London.
  • In Milan and São Paulo, queries are rising for seamstress repairs and DIY alterations.

Check out the full Fashion Capitals Trends Report here.

entries.title: We’re supporting nature restoration through sustainable farming in Brazil.
entries.summary: Google is partnering with Working Trees to remove 270,000 tons of CO2 via silvopasture in Brazil. See how this project restores land and ranching.
entries.content:
Today, through the Symbiosis Coalition, we’re announcing a long-term agreement with Working Trees to remove 270,000 tons of carbon dioxide through their project in Brazil.

Working Trees plants trees directly on active pasturelands across Brazil’s Amazon and Cerrado biomes, a practice called silvopasture that restores ranchland without displacing cattle. In addition to removing CO₂, this gives ranchers an opportunity to diversify their income through timber and carbon revenues. As the trees grow, they provide much-needed shade to the cattle, enhancing both soil health and drought resilience, and ultimately boosting land and livestock productivity.

The approach provides a highly scalable solution, with the potential to expand across millions of hectares of Brazilian ranchlands. It also uses Working Trees' advanced digital platform to enable ranchers to track every single tree planted, creating a transparent verification trail to monitor impact. It’s a great example of technology helping both people and the planet.

entries.title: We’re sharing 3 tips to study smarter with Gemini Notebook.
entries.summary: Master your exams with Google Gemini Notebook’s new 60-second video overviews and interactive quiz formats. Try these study tools at notebook.google.
entries.content:
Studying for exams can feel overwhelming. To help you prepare, we recently launched three new features in Gemini Notebook to make your learning more structured and engaging.

  • Short Video Overviews: If you’re trying to quickly grasp a tricky concept, you can now generate a 60-second Short Video Overview to help you unpack it. They’re easy to watch on-the-go or share with a classmate.
  • Interactive Learning Overviews: If you have dozens of notes, lectures, and readings to review, you can create an Interactive Learning Overview under Reports to walk you through your material, step by step. It weaves together summaries and studio outputs like slides, quizzes, and flashcards, all grounded strictly in your coursework.
  • Expanded quiz formats: We also added more ways for you to test your knowledge with new quiz formats, including short-answer, multi-select, and fill-in-the blank options. After testing yourself or reviewing your flashcards, you can ask your notebook for feedback to pinpoint where you should focus next.

Try them with your own materials at notebook.google.
